speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that; to begin our investigation, can you tell me exactly how long you've had these blisters and ulcers, and have they appeared on any other parts of your body besides the forearm and mouth?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent start on captopril and the combination of blisters and mucosal ulcers, I need to confirm if the skin lesions are specifically on your palms or soles, and whether you have experienced any fever or swollen glands since the rash began. Additionally, please describe the appearance of the ulcers in your mouth—are they shallow or deep, and do they have a red halo?

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) secondary to Captopril allergy.
